text: In a small bowl, mix the yeast and sugar with a tablespoon of warm water to activate.
Leave this for 5 minutes in a warm place.
In a separate bowl, mix the flour, onion seeds, salt and baking powder.
Once the yeast is frothy, add this to the flour mixture with some oil and yoghurt.
Begin to knead the dough with slightly wet hands, folding as you go.
If the dough feels dry, add a little splash of milk and continue to knead.
Once the dough is nice and soft, cover with a little bit of oil and some cling film and leave in a warm place to rise for about an hour.
To make the Peshawari filling, place the pistachios and raisins into a blender and blitz to create a coarse powder, almost like sand.
Turn the grill on to a high heat and divide the dough into 4 balls.
Take a large pinch of the powder and place at the centre of one of the dough balls.
Start to fold the dough around the powder to enclose it inside.
To about half a centimetre thick.
Heat the traditional tawa or a frying pan and place the naan onto it for a couple of seconds to brown on one side.
Transfer the naan to a baking sheet and place under a hot grill for between 2 to 5 minutes and watch the magic as they puff up.
Once cooked, smear with a little bit of butter.
